title: Rehearsal in the classroom
author: Jo Castelino
summary: Castelino describes a recurring problem: students seem to recall facts in lessons yet mix up key terms and fail to link ideas in end-of-topic assessments. Using a Year 10 biology lesson on the heart, she diagnoses a lack of rehearsal, specifically verbal practice of whole sequences before retrieval practice, following Tom Sherrington. Saying the full path of blood through the heart aloud embeds terms in context rather than as isolated words. She sets out a concrete routine of telling, memorising, volunteers, cold calling and stopping mid-sentence, with turn-and-talk for larger classes. She adds that it only works in a classroom culture where mistakes are safe.
points: Recall of isolated facts in lessons does not guarantee students can link them or use the right terms later.
Verbal rehearsal of whole sequences should come before retrieval practice and secures terms in context.
A small-class routine of cold calling and mid-sentence handoffs keeps every student engaged.
Larger classes can use turn and talk followed by a few students rehearsing aloud.
Rehearsal depends on a supportive culture where students are unafraid of mistakes.
quotes: During lessons, students appear to recall key facts. They get to practice writing these facts and linking them to other facts when answering questions independently in lessons and at home, through homework. Why, then, do they struggle to link things well and mix up key terms in assessments?

In the above scenario, students can recall simple facts but verbalising sequences that link those facts together is also needed. The latter also has the advantage of consolidating key terms securely within the right context.

Most importantly, when students rehearse saying this sequence out loud, they remember all the facts in context. They are not just remembering the word ‘aorta’ as the vessel that carries oxygentaed blood away from the heart but in the context of the flow of blood and even suggests its location by saying that blood is flowing ‘up and out’ of the heart.
Rehearsing important sequences and links between concepts empowers students. We are not just limiting them to recall of one-word answers.
Next, I ask for volunteers and pick on a couple of confident students. This gives the others a bit more time to remember the key parts.
You do need the right culture in your classroom before rehearsal in this manner works. Students should be supportive of each other and not afraid to make mistakes.
